title: Naturality of Spec kappa(x) -> X; open immersions induce isomorphisms of residue fields
statement: Let $g:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $x\in X$, and for a point $z$ of a scheme $Z$ let $j_z:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)\to Z$ be the canonical morphism ($\operatorname{Spec}$ of the residue map $\mathcal O_{Z,z}\to\kappa(z)$ followed by $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{Z,z}\to Z$) [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $r:\kappa(g(x))\to\kappa(x)$ be the map induced by $g$ on residue fields. Then $g\circ j_x=j_{g(x)}\circ\operatorname{Spec}(r)$. If $g$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], $r$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Schemes, section Points of schemes (Tag 01J5), the commutative diagram after Lemma Tag 01J9 (lemma-characterize-points, lines 2478-2498: Spec(kappa(x)) -> Spec(O_{X,x}) -> X over Spec(kappa(s)) -> Spec(O_{S,s}) -> S); for open immersions Lemma Tag 01HH (lemma-open-immersion, line 241: an open immersion is an isomorphism onto an open subspace, so it induces isomorphisms of local rings and of residue fields)
